record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Role of short- versus long-term memory
record.original_question: In movement models with both short-term and long-term memory layers, where the two memory variables have different uptake and decay rates and influence movement through a combined advective potential, what distinct roles do short-term and long-term memory play in well-posedness and in the form of steady states? More generally, can the inclusion of both memory layers produce space-use effects that do not arise when only one layer is present?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 32. What role does short vs. long-term memory play in differing modelling scenarios, e.g., the well-posedness of problems or influences on steady state profiles? Are both short and long-term memory components necessary and/or sufficient to predict certain space use phenomena, if ever? That is, does the inclusion of both short and long-term memory produce novel effects not found when only, say, short-term memory is included?

artifact.category_tag: nonlocal PDE models for animal movement with memory
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a class of advection–diffusion PDE models for animal movement of the form

  u_t = ∇·(D ∇u − u ∇P(k_s, k_ℓ)),   x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ^n, t > 0,

where u(x,t) ≥ 0 is the density of animals, D > 0 is a diffusion coefficient, and the advective potential P depends on two distinct memory fields:

• a short-term memory variable k_s(x,t), satisfying an uptake–decay equation
   ∂_t k_s = α_s u − β_s k_s,
• a long-term memory variable k_ℓ(x,t), satisfying
   ∂_t k_ℓ = α_ℓ u − β_ℓ k_ℓ,

with uptake rates α_s, α_ℓ > 0 and decay rates β_s, β_ℓ > 0 satisfying β_s ≫ β_ℓ (so that k_s fades quickly while k_ℓ persists). The advective potential P may be a (possibly nonlocal) functional of both memory layers, e.g. P = γ_s G_s * k_s + γ_ℓ G_ℓ * k_ℓ for suitable spatial kernels G_s, G_ℓ and weights γ_s, γ_ℓ.

Address the following:

(a) Determine the distinct contributions of the short-term memory variable k_s and the long-term memory variable k_ℓ to well-posedness (existence, uniqueness, regularity, and global-in-time bounds) of the coupled system in suitable function spaces on Ω with prescribed boundary and initial conditions.

(b) Characterize how each memory layer separately shapes the structure of nontrivial steady states (u*, k_s*, k_ℓ*), including their existence, multiplicity, spatial profile (e.g. concentration, aggregation, or home-range formation), and bifurcation behavior with respect to the parameters.

(c) Decide whether the simultaneous inclusion of both memory layers can produce qualitative space-use phenomena—such as patterns, transient dynamics, or stationary distributions—that cannot be reproduced by a corresponding model containing only one of the two memory variables.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research question concerning the joint role of short- and long-term memory layers in nonlocal PDE animal-movement models. A web search does not reveal a published resolution; related works develop single-memory advection–diffusion models with cognitive mapping but do not give a definitive comparative theory of dual-memory effects on well-posedness, steady states, and space-use phenomena.
